---
title: "Delivery times with Plotfoundry"
format: html
resources:
  - node_modules/plotfoundry/**
---

This document uses the locally installed JavaScript package and its bundled Plot.
No Python or R engine is used. Serve the rendered directory over local HTTP.

```{ojs}
pf = import(new URL("./node_modules/plotfoundry/src/index.js", document.baseURI).href)
adapter = import(new URL("./node_modules/plotfoundry/src/observable.js", document.baseURI).href)
spec = pf.loadSpec()
config = pf.theme(spec, "tufte", {mode: "light", profile: "reading"})
fonts = {
  const session = await adapter.loadFonts(config);
  invalidation.then(() => session.dispose());
  return session;
}
observations = ["North", "Central", "South"].flatMap((route, i) =>
  [1,2,3,4,5,6].map((week, j) => ({route, week,
    hours: route === "Central" && week === 3 ? null :
      [2.2,2.6,2.4,2.1,1.8,1.9][j] + i * 2.3})))
```

North improves after week four. Central has no observation in week three;
the gap does not mean zero hours. South stays slower throughout this invented example.

```{ojs}
{
  fonts;
  const chart = adapter.plot(config, {
    height: 384,
    x: {label: "Week"},
    y: {label: "Delivery time (hours)", domain: [0,10]},
    marks: adapter.line(config, observations, {
      x: "week", y: "hours", category: "route",
      domain: ["North", "Central", "South"]
    })
  });
  adapter.stylePlot(config, chart);
  return chart;
}
```

The canvas is 640 CSS pixels wide. Change the mode or profile in `config` to
compare light/dark or reading/presentation output. A fit-to-page preview reduces
all marks and text together; use the declared width to judge the placed sizes.
